verdicts.reason: Flat orthographic node-link graph: dark boxes (Root CA, Issuing CA 1/2, 1SN0S.LAB, RDP01, WEB01, pki, CLIENT01) joined by straight grey connector lines. No desk, no user, no night-lit scene, no depth, no key or rim light. All six strip frames are the same image except the caption plate fading in.

No amber pulse and no floor channel. The camera is static and does not follow anything. The B-01.2 a and b frames are byte-identical to B-01.1 b. The straight lines from CLIENT01 to RDP01 and WEB01 are static connectors.
There is no arrival and no listener lighting up. RDP01 is an unchanged dark rectangle. Only the caption changes, so this is a slide with a caption.
No self-signed card, no self-seal, no unverified state, no amber pulse dying out. All three frames are byte-identical. The beat's accuracy content is not shown.
No RDPAuth badge drops in. There is no motion from AD to RDP01. Opacity-only caption change; the scene is otherwise unchanged.
No key pair forms and there is no server chassis. The only change is the caption fading in, and the caption text is scored through by connector lines.
No locked key container and no lock motif. All three frames are byte-identical to the end of B-03.1.
No glass capsule, public key or request information. Only the caption text swaps. The caption overprints the connector lines and is partly illegible.
No beam and no seal. Frames a and b are byte-identical. Nothing is emitted from a key.

No capsule at the outbound port, no steel-blue lookup pulse and no lit route to CA 1. AD (1SN0S.LAB) is a plain box with straight connectors to Issuing CA 1/2 and RDP/WEB. This is a static topology diagram, and the connectors even imply AD sits on the path to the CAs.
No capsule travels into the CA 1 vault, no cyan, no lit route. The identical static image repeats.
The four staggered check ticks are absent. All three frames are byte-identical. The caption 'Issuing CA 1 verifies, then signs' is double-struck by connector lines running through the glyphs.
No press, no sealed key module and no stamped certificate card (SAN, EKU, validity bar). The beat has no visible content.
No certificate locks in beside the key and no translucent intermediate copy settles. No caption, and the screen is the bare node graph.

No crane up, no gold sealed vault on a plinth, no self-signed ring or light sweep. The Root CA is a small dark text box at the top of the graph, with two connector lines running to it, which contradicts AR-01's 'no cables'.

The 'flashback' is the same graph with the box fills turned neutral grey (f1245 vs f1246). Camera, layout and content are unchanged, so it is a recolour rather than a motivated cut. There is no setup scene, removable media, CA request with CA=true band or tag, or root signing.

Return from the flashback is only a fill colour change back to navy. There is no gold-to-cyan trust link growing, and the connectors drawn between nodes are static straight lines, exactly the diagram grammar C-01 forbids.
No fresh amber pulse, no certificate cards or handshake proof travelling to the client. The strip is byte-identical to the B-04.5 and B-05.1 strips, so nothing moves.
No cards dock upward into a chain and there is no gold root shimmer. The caption 'The client validates the whole chain' is mangled by the lines passing through it.
No AIA indicator. Four identical frames, with a=b=c byte-identical to the end of B-06.2.
The six staggered checks, with the sixth pending, are absent. a and b are byte-identical. The 20 s validation scene shows nothing that validates.
No amber CRL scroll fetches, no 'OCSP if deployed' tag. Static graph. No amber appears anywhere in the film.

There is no amber-to-green channel change and no session window. The caption 'Trusted RDP connection established' is shown over unchanged grey-white lines, with connector strokes running through its glyphs. The payoff is a caption only.
There is no camera glide to WEB01 and no WebServer-TLS badge. WEB01 is the same small box. The strip is byte-identical to the B-04.5 strip.
No key pair, no locked key, no sealed request. Still graph.

CA 1 does not dim to grey and CA 2 does not light violet. There are no eligibility tags. a, b and c are byte-identical. The caption 'Different templates can use different issuing CAs' overprints CLIENT01 and the connector lines, and the strokes cut through the glyphs.
No capsule travels to Issuing CA 2. The scene has no moving subject.
There are no compressed checks and no 'name supplied in request' note. Unchanged still.
No violet press and no TLS certificate stamped. No copy of the CA certificate. Only the caption text changes.

There is no gold link revealing CA 2's certificate joining the same root. The pre-existing static connector from Issuing CA 2 to the Root is the only link. The strip is byte-identical to the B-04.5 strip.
No browser validation, no docking, no CRL fetches, no green channel. The strip is byte-identical to the B-04.5 strip. A 5 s validation beat is invisible.

The 'hero topology' is the same flat front-on graph used from frame 4 onward. It is not a wide hero shot with a camera move. There are no cyan, violet or gold trust paths converging on a root, and the root is a text box tied by straight connectors. Caption 'Different issuing paths. One trusted root.' is struck through by lines.

The title card is a flat label plate placed on top of the same node graph, which dims and fades to black. There is no settle motion. The final black frame is clean but the film does not end on anything cinematic.

findings.evidence: Every shot is a flat graph: rectangular text boxes joined by straight, static, hairline grey connectors (Root to CA1/CA2, CA1/CA2 to 1SN0S.LAB, 1SN0S.LAB to RDP01/WEB01, pki to CLIENT01, CLIENT01 to RDP01/WEB01). The connectors are already present at frame 4 and never grow or flow.
findings.why: This is the diagram grammar C-01 forbids: static straight connectors between nodes, not network channels or trust links that grow or flow when introduced. All 33 shots are DIAGRAM. At Stage 4 and later a DIAGRAM shot is a BLOCKER.
findings.direction: Remove node-and-line drawing entirely. Show relationships through grounded objects, channels, docking, light and camera moves. Any line must be a channel or trust link that grows when introduced.

findings.evidence: The same front-on layout of dark navy rectangles with small monospace labels sits in the middle of an empty black frame for all 109 s, with caption plates swapped on top. No perspective depth cues, no environment, no 3D forms.
findings.why: Reads as a slide or template. Spec requires a perspective beauty camera in a night-lit space, and no frame may be a regular flat card layout facing the camera.
findings.direction: Build a staged 3D scene with a perspective camera, a lit environment and real objects (desk, rack, vaults, capsules, cards) that the beats act on.

findings.evidence: The camera never moves. Node positions are pixel-identical in every strip frame of every beat. Beats that require following (B-01.2), a crane up (B-05.1), a glide (B-07.1) and a wide hero shot (B-09.2) have no camera motion.
findings.why: No camera move at all means no parallax and no camera that leads or follows the action. The only visible change between frames is caption opacity and fill colour.
findings.direction: Animate one continuous camera with eased follow, crane and glide moves that frame each focal subject.

findings.evidence: No focal subject is distinguishable in any beat. All nodes have equal weight, equal brightness and no depth of field. Beats such as B-04.3 (four checks) and B-06.4 (validation checks) show nothing that could be a subject.
findings.why: Every shot needs one clear focal subject established by DOF, light and composition. Here a viewer's eye lands on the caption or nothing.
findings.direction: Frame one declared subject per beat with focus, key light and composition; push everything else back with DOF and lower light.

findings.evidence: None of the persistent narrative objects appears in any frame: no request capsules, certificate cards, key pairs, key container, vaults, template badge, press, handshake proof, CRL scroll, AIA indicator, validation ticks, or green/amber/violet/cyan/gold state. Beats B-02.2 to B-09.1 are pixel-identical to a still image except captions.
findings.why: The animatic does not stage the story at all, and content beats cannot be judged FILM. A large part of the spec's visible content (including the PKI accuracy constraints) is absent, so the animatic cannot show continuity of persistent objects.
findings.direction: Animate every spec beat's objects: capsules, cards, keys and containers, vaults, presses and links, each with a proper entrance and exit.

findings.evidence: The palette is a single navy and grey. Root is not gold, CA 1 not cyan, CA 2 not violet, AD not steel blue; there is no amber, no green on trusted completion and no grey for the ineligible CA 1 in B-07.3.
findings.why: The colour language carries state changes (pending to trusted, ineligible route, which CA signed). With no colour roles, state cannot be read and the C-10 role tokens are unused. L-07 distinguishability cannot be met either.
findings.direction: Apply the role palette: gold root, cyan CA 1, violet CA 2, steel-blue AD, neutral-white requests, amber pending, green only after validation, grey ineligible.

findings.evidence: Flat unlit fills, no shading, no key or rim, no luminance falloff, no shadow side on any object. The background is pure black.
findings.why: No motivated lighting. A 'night-lit desk' and 'gold vault' mood is impossible without lit-side to shadow-side ratio on a subject.
findings.direction: Light each scene with a motivated key and a rim or back light, and shade the focal subject.

findings.evidence: The only entrances in the film are caption plate fades and the plate colour swap at f1246/f1396. There are no object entrances with location or scale and emission, only opacity changes (the B-09.3 strip shows opacity fading of the whole graph).
findings.why: Opacity-only entrances. The spec requires entrances animating at least two of location, scale and emission, with eased exits slightly faster than entrances.
findings.direction: Give every object entrance location plus scale or emission motion with Bezier easing, and exits 0.6 to 0.9 times the entrance duration.

findings.evidence: At the two cut frames the geometry, camera and layout are identical; only box fills change from navy to grey and back. The flashback has no distinct place or time apart from a desaturation.
findings.why: The single motivated hard cut is the only permitted cut and must read as an earlier time and place. A recolour with no new scene does not motivate or sell a flashback and does not show the offline ceremony.
findings.direction: Stage the flashback as a different, clearly earlier setup scene (removable media, the CA request, the root signing), with the camera cutting in and out.

findings.evidence: Caption text is struck through by the grey connector lines that run from CLIENT01 up to RDP01, WEB01 and pki, and it overlaps the CLIENT01 box. Text looks doubled or cut ('Issuing CA 1 verifies, then signs', 'Trusted RDP connection established', 'Different issuing paths. One trusted root.') and in B-06.2 reads as 'The client vaidites the whole chain'. The captions sit at about y=480 of 540, over diagram content.
findings.why: Captions are partly illegible and cover lower-left graph content (CLIENT01 is the user node). The caption appears to be composited under the connector strokes, which breaks L-02 contrast and L-05 clearance.
findings.direction: Place the caption in a dedicated, clean lower band over a solid plate above all scene geometry, clear of the focal action.

findings.evidence: All boxes and lines sit on a single plane, with no foreground element, no background plane and no parallax. The scene occupies only the centre 35% of the frame width; the left and right thirds are empty black.
findings.why: No foreground, midground and background layers, and no parallax because the camera never moves. The composition is also off-balance and wastes frame.
findings.direction: Compose with real depth layers and a camera move that produces visible parallax.

findings.evidence: In-world labels (1SN0S.LAB, RDP01, WEB01, pki.1sn0s.lab, CLIENT01) are about 6 to 8 px high at 960x540 (about 12 to 16 px at 1080p) and are overlapped by connector lines, so they are readable but small. They are always on screen, even when they should matter only at specific beats.
findings.why: Names should be readable at 18 px or more at 1080p when they matter. The 'RDP01' and 'WEB01' labels are crossed by lines.
findings.direction: Raise must-read label cap height to at least 18 px at 1080p and keep lines clear of them.
